gen_risks.description: GORE Arequipa lacks experience with World Bank‑financed projects, risking fiduciary and implementation shortcomings.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted capacity‑building, early recruitment of key staff, and close supervision on fiduciary and environmental safeguards.
gen_risks.evidence: GORE does not have experience implementing WB‑financed projects, so capacity building and close supervision will be required.

gen_risks.description: Delayed recruitment of financial management staff could postpone project start‑up and disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare terms of reference early and appoint all FM positions, including FM specialist, within two months of effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Delayed recruitment of FM staff... all the FM staff shall be appointed within two months after effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Budget allocation and execution delays common in Peru may hinder project readiness and cash flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate budget allocation immediately after loan signing and follow the Project Operations Manual for timely execution.
gen_risks.evidence: initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates.

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate accounting and financial reporting due to limited experience with WB procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use the national accounting system (SIAF), conduct annual independent audits, and train staff on WB financial standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential inaccuracies in accounting and financial reporting... national accounting system (SIAF) will be used... supplemented by annual independent audits.

gen_risks.description: Fragmented coordination among ministries, municipalities and private sector may cause implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish high‑level steering and consultative committees with clear TORs, schedule regular meetings and joint decision‑making.
gen_risks.evidence: high‑level steering and consultative committees are expected to be formed to oversee and support project implementation.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related hazards (floods, landslides, earthquakes) could damage roads and heritage sites.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate‑resilient designs, slope stabilization, drainage, and consider insurance schemes for high‑risk assets.
gen_risks.evidence: main climate and natural hazard risks... heavy rains, flooding, landslides, high seismic activity.

gen_risks.description: Construction in landslide‑prone zones may lead to cost overruns and schedule slips.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct detailed geotechnical surveys, avoid high‑risk alignments, and apply engineered mitigation measures where unavoidable.
gen_risks.evidence: Subcomponent 2.1 addresses the vulnerability of transportation infrastructure to floods and landslides.

gen_risks.description: Water and sanitation upgrades may lack sustainable operation & maintenance, reducing service quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop O&M manuals, train local operators, and establish dedicated maintenance funds for the new facilities.
gen_risks.evidence: project will support arrangements that ensure mechanisms are in place for the ongoing maintenance and sustainability of the improved assets.

gen_risks.description: Reforestation targets may not be achieved, limiting carbon‑sequestration benefits.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement robust monitoring, involve community groups in planting and care, and secure funding for seedlings and maintenance.
gen_risks.evidence: Reforestation of Bosque de Queñua is completed... mitigation measures include reforestation of degraded forest areas.

gen_risks.description: Risk of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment affecting women participants and project reputation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce the SEA/SH Action Plan, provide mandatory training, and operate a grievance mechanism with swift response.
gen_risks.evidence: project’s action plan on sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH) will address barriers.

gen_risks.description: Procurement of numerous small works may not fully comply with World Bank procurement rules.
gen_risks.mitigation: Follow WB Procurement Regulations, use standard documents, and conduct internal procurement reviews before award.
gen_risks.evidence: Project procurement will follow the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’.

gen_risks.description: Private investors may postpone commitments if public infrastructure is delayed or of insufficient quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align public works timelines with private investment pipelines, provide clear investment opportunities, and use Obras por Impuestos incentives.
gen_risks.evidence: private sector ... is willing to invest once they see that infrastructure and tourism offerings are upgraded.

gen_risks.description: Tourism demand forecasts could be overly optimistic, reducing projected economic returns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct periodic demand reviews, adjust marketing strategies, and diversify tourism products to mitigate shortfalls.
gen_risks.evidence: Market demand analysis indicates substantial tourism growth potential... projected growth rates.

gen_risks.description: Recent political instability may affect government commitment and funding continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year budget commitments, embed the project in legal frameworks, and maintain high‑level political advocacy.
gen_risks.evidence: increased political instability in recent years.

gen_risks.description: High road fatality rate raises safety risks for construction crews and future road users.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict safety protocols, worker training, traffic management plans, and install road safety features (guardrails, markings).
gen_risks.evidence: Arequipa region has sustained a higher road fatality rate... designs will also include road safety features.

gen_risks.description: Construction of the Yura health centre may experience cost overruns or schedule delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed construction schedule with contingencies, monitor progress weekly, and allocate a cost contingency reserve.
gen_risks.evidence: subcomponent 2.3 Health ... finance demolition of the existing health clinic, construction of a larger clinic.

gen_risks.description: Disbursement is blocked until three Interinstitutional Agreements are signed, risking cash‑flow gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Negotiate agreements early, set internal deadlines, and monitor signing status to meet the Bank’s condition.
gen_risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made ... unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements.

gen_risks.description: Work in Salinas and Aguada Blanca National Reserve may breach protected‑area regulations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Obtain SERNANP approvals, prepare an Environmental and Social Management Plan, and conduct regular compliance monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: coordination with SERNANP for work in the Salinas and Aguada Blanca National Reserve.

gen_risks.description: Capacity‑building activities may not translate into effective destination management.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include post‑training coaching, performance indicators, and periodic evaluations of institutional capacity gains.
gen_risks.evidence: capacity building for destination management will focus on strengthening the capacity of GORE.

gen_risks.description: M&E data may be incomplete or inaccurate due to reliance on surveys and remote‑sensing methods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish robust data‑collection protocols, backup data sources, and conduct regular data‑quality audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Monitoring will leverage data collection mechanisms from existing sources ... will include dedicated surveys.

gen_risks.description: Existing gender wage gap may limit women’s economic benefits despite project interventions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide targeted entrepreneurship training, monitor gender‑wage indicators, and promote women‑led enterprises in tourism.
gen_risks.evidence: Peru also has a large gender wage gap, estimated at 25 percent in 2021.

gen_risks.description: Failure to create and staff the PIU within 60 days breaches loan covenants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare a recruitment plan with clear timelines and monitor staffing milestones against the covenant deadline.
gen_risks.evidence: personnel to be hired ... no later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Accelerating climate change may exceed design assumptions, shortening asset lifespan.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate adaptive management, periodic climate‑risk reassessments, and design with safety margins.
gen_risks.evidence: climate change will likely exacerbate existing regional disparities by increasing the impacts and frequency of natural hazards.

gen_risks.description: Potential conflicts with indigenous communities over land or cultural sites could delay works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes and engage communities early in project planning.
gen_risks.evidence: FPIC; Indigenous Peoples Plan (IPP) listed among abbreviations.

gen_risks.description: Historically low budget execution rates may reduce available funds for project components.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict budget tracking, quarterly execution reviews, and incentives for timely spending.
gen_risks.evidence: initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates.

gt_risks.description: Peru is in a period of substantial political uncertainty (low popular support for the executive and Congress, high political fragmentation); a new government assumes office July 2026 and regional elections are scheduled October 2026. Since GORE Arequipa (a regional government) is the implementing agency, regional government changes could slow implementation or shift priorities; high-level changes at MINCETUR could also affect oversight commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focus on highly needed, consensus-driven investments; maintain buy-in and continuous dialogue with the tourism private sector; engage proactively with any new authorities on project opportunities; use implementation arrangements that are technically strong, highly competent, and relatively shielded from political influence and staff turnover.

gt_risks.description: Tourism projects are inherently complex, involving infrastructure, capacity building, and multiple government levels/sectors plus private-sector and community stakeholders. Capacity must be built at GORE Arequipa given no precedent for multisectoral regional investment programs in Peru, and historic national-regional coordination weaknesses. The project also does not budget for O&M of delivered sites/infrastructure, which falls to designated stakeholders.
gt_risks.mitigation: Institutional capacity building via the Project (incl. GFPP) to ready GORE for implementation; World Bank support on PIU composition and key staff selection; coordination arrangements/agreements between the PIU and local partners in charge of operating sites, to align on design, implementation, and handover.

gt_risks.description: Combined fiduciary risk with GORE Arequipa is Substantial, reflecting the entity's lack of prior experience with World Bank or other MDB-financed operations in both financial management and procurement.
gt_risks.mitigation: A fiduciary assessment identified capacity gaps and informed mitigation measures; recruit dedicated FM and Procurement Specialists supported by qualified administrative staff; detail minimum FM/procurement procedures aligned with WB requirements in the Project Operational Manual; use SIAF for financial transactions/reporting and STEP for procurement planning/monitoring; targeted WB training, regular fiduciary supervision, and annual audits.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk reflects the scope/nature of planned interventions, works located in environmentally and culturally sensitive areas, and GORE Arequipa's limited institutional capacity to manage risks per the Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthen PIU capacity to manage E&S risks with adequate resources/staffing; elaborate and implement project-level instruments (Stakeholder Engagement Plan, Labor Management Plan, SEA/SH Plan) plus intervention-level instruments with specific mitigation measures.
